newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bank Melbourne deal lifts Westpac shares.
newsitem.headline: Bank Melbourne deal lifts Westpac shares.

text.p: Shares in Westpac Banking Corp were up 32 cents at a record high A$8.55 in active trade on Monday with an upbeat assessment of its Bank of Melbourne bid deal boosting sentiment for the stock.
Westpac received regulatory approval for the deal from the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) on Friday, although the ACCC required some undertakings from Westpac.

Westpac is offering A$9.75 a share for Bank of Melbourne, including a 90 cents fully franked special dividend with the balance of A$8.85 to be paid in cash or as one Westpac share and up to A$1.85 in cash.
"There has been a lot of positive sentiment about the stock now the bid has been approved," said a dealer at a Sydney brokerage.

Macquarie Equities banking analyst Graham Maloney agreed the deal was a winner for the New South Wales-based major, pointing to Westpac's vulnerability in Australia's second most populous state without the acquisition.
"The bank had declared themselves as very exposed if they didn't get it and it was marked down a bit for that. Now it has come through, the shares have kicked back up again," he said.
Westpac outperformed the broader market, posting a 3.7 percent gain against the buoyant broader market's gain of 1.2 percent.
By 3.00 p.m. (0500 GMT), Westpac shares were off their highs to be up 30 cents at A$8.53 with 4.7 million shares traded.
